name: Chamber of Parhedrin (High Priest's Pre-Yom Kippur Quarters)
notes: The chamber where the High Priest was sequestered for seven days before Yom Kippur; its laws and practices

name: High Priest's Seven-Day Preparation for Yom Kippur
notes: The seven-day sequestering, practice of service, and preparation of the High Priest before Yom Kippur

name: Designating a Replacement Wife for the High Priest
notes: The debate whether to designate a replacement wife for the High Priest lest his wife die before Yom Kippur, based on 'his house' meaning his wife

name: Priestly Lottery (Payis) for Temple Service
notes: The four daily lotteries conducted in the Temple to determine which priests perform the various services; history of how the lottery replaced a race after injury

name: Oath Administered to the High Priest Before Yom Kippur
notes: The oath administered by the elders to the High Priest that he would not deviate from the prescribed Yom Kippur service, particularly regarding incense in the Holy of Holies

name: Keeping the High Priest Awake on Yom Kippur Eve
notes: The practices used to prevent the High Priest from sleeping on Yom Kippur eve, including Torah reading, snapping fingers, and standing on cold floor

name: Confession (Vidui) on Yom Kippur
notes: The three confessions recited by the High Priest on Yom Kippur: over his bull (for himself and family), again over the bull (adding the priests), and over the scapegoat (for all Israel)

name: Utterance of the Explicit Divine Name (Shem HaMephorash)
notes: The High Priest's utterance of the Tetragrammaton on Yom Kippur during the confessions; the people's response 'Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom'

name: Lots for the Two Yom Kippur Goats (Goralot)
notes: The lottery procedure to designate which goat is for God and which for Azazel; the lottery receptacle and its historical development from wood to gold

name: Incense Offering in the Holy of Holies
notes: The unique Yom Kippur incense service performed inside the Holy of Holies; the coal pan, spoon, handfuls of incense, procedure of entry and exit

name: Blood Sprinklings on Yom Kippur
notes: The specific blood sprinklings of Yom Kippur: inside the Holy of Holies (one up, seven down), on the parochet, and on the golden altar; counting method

name: Foundation Stone (Even HaShtiya)
notes: The foundation rock in the Holy of Holies from the days of the early prophets, three fingerbreadths high, upon which the High Priest placed the incense after the Ark was taken

name: Dispatching the Scapegoat to the Wilderness
notes: The procedure of leading the scapegoat to the cliff (Tzuk), the booths along the route, the crimson strip, the escort, and the signal system back to Jerusalem

name: Crimson Strip (Lashon shel Zehorit)
notes: The crimson strip tied to the scapegoat's horns and to the sanctuary entrance; its miraculous turning white when sins were forgiven

name: Burning the Bull and Goat of Yom Kippur
hebrew: שריפת הפר והשעיר של יום הכיפורים
notes: The procedure of burning the bull and goat sin-offerings outside Jerusalem; when their carriers become impure

name: Torah Reading by the High Priest on Yom Kippur
hebrew: קריאת התורה של כהן גדול ביום הכיפורים
notes: The High Priest's public Torah reading on Yom Kippur from Leviticus 16 and 23; the eight blessings he recites afterward

name: Five Afflictions on Yom Kippur (Inuyim)
notes: The five prohibitions constituting affliction on Yom Kippur: eating/drinking, bathing, anointing, wearing shoes, and conjugal relations; their measures and exceptions

name: Measures for Eating/Drinking on Yom Kippur
notes: The date-bulk measure for food and cheekful measure for drink that create liability on Yom Kippur; whether food and drink combine

name: Training Minors to Fast (Chinuch for Yom Kippur)
notes: The practice of training children one or two years before bar/bat mitzvah to fast partial fasts on Yom Kippur

name: Saving Life (Pikuach Nefesh) Overriding Yom Kippur
notes: Cases where danger to life overrides Yom Kippur fasting: pregnant women with cravings, the ill, bulmos sufferers, rockslide victims

name: Bulmos (Life-Threatening Hunger Illness)
notes: The medical condition of severe hunger causing vision impairment; one may feed the sufferer even impure food until his eyes recover

name: Scope of Yom Kippur Atonement
notes: What Yom Kippur atones for: transgressions between person and God vs. between people; requirement to appease others; the interplay between sin-offering, guilt-offering, death, repentance and Yom Kippur

name: Atonement for Interpersonal Sins (Bein Adam laChavero)
hebrew: כפרה על עבירות שבין אדם לחברו
notes: The principle that Yom Kippur does not atone for sins between people until one appeases the offended party

name: Repentance and Its Role in Atonement
notes: The graduated system of atonement: repentance for minor sins, Yom Kippur for severe ones, death for gravest; the invalid who says 'I will sin and repent'

name: Device for Sinking the Temple Basin (Mukheni)
notes: The mechanical device built by ben Katin to sink the Temple laver into water overnight to prevent its water from being disqualified by remaining overnight

name: Temple Benefactors and Their Contributions
notes: Those who contributed to the Temple: Yehoshua ben Gamla (gold lots), ben Katin (mukheni, spigots), King Munbaz (gold handles), Queen Helene (chandelier, golden tablet), Nicanor (doors). Contrasted with those who withheld secrets: House of Garmu, House of Avtinas, Hugras ben Levi, ben Kamtzar

name: House of Avtinas (Incense Preparers)
notes: The family that held the secret formula for preparing the Temple incense and refused to teach it to others

name: House of Garmu (Shewbread Bakers)
notes: The family that held the secret of preparing the shewbread and refused to teach it to others

name: High Priest's Five Immersions and Ten Sanctifications on Yom Kippur
hebrew: חמש טבילות ועשר קידושין של כהן גדול
notes: The five immersions and ten sanctifications of hands and feet performed by the High Priest throughout the Yom Kippur service; where each is performed

name: White Linen Garments of the High Priest on Yom Kippur
notes: The special white linen garments worn by the High Priest during Yom Kippur's inner services (Holy of Holies); their cost, origin (Pelusium vs. India), and alternation with golden garments

name: Order of the Yom Kippur Service (Seder HaAvodah)
notes: The precise sequential order of all Yom Kippur services; consequence of performing them out of order; need to repeat services if blood spills

name: Gate of Nicanor
notes: The famous gate of the Temple named after Nicanor; the miracle associated with its doors

name: Signal System from Wilderness to Temple
notes: The system of platforms and waving scarves used to signal from the wilderness back to Jerusalem when the scapegoat arrived; debate about its necessity
